answer: Write-triggered cache invalidation depends on the authoritative write path emitting a reliable invalidation/change signal that the cache can observe (a defined owning writer and change event/version). When changes cannot be reliably signaled, no reliable invalidation path exists: write-triggered invalidation is contraindicated because readers can miss the signal or briefly see stale data after a write, and expiration after a configured period (TTL-based expiration) is the bounded-staleness alternative.
